{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-az-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"9b2ed94695a28127716aa2daa702e5bf1492e204f684b1fdebab7dcc2cdf0bfb","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-az-class-d:lineage:128","source_registry_sha256":"6dbbc2d22fea619728bdb90038a4aedf3afc07eab652b3f97027c9c69aaadaf4","source_liveness_sha256":"1c5753487760cbe2044d84b5696121c7181af61815b598d89d5ce158abf5fe43"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Following-distance, blind-spot, signaling and passing confusables","heading":"C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: the count versus the cushion range, tailgaters, blind spots, signal distance and timing, passing left and right","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: the count versus the cushion range, tailgaters, blind spots, signal distance and timing, passing left and right
Look-alike numbers and rules from the space-cushion, signaling and passing pages, each tied to one handbook page; hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec06-R01 | anchor: A01
The count in the example runs to four and takes about 4 seconds, while the cushion the manual recommends in poor conditions spans 3 to 6 seconds. [A01]
Why it matters: group following distance; difficulty three; confusable sec06-F07 versus sec06-F09.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R02 | anchor: A01
Following distance is counted in seconds behind the vehicle ahead, while bicycle clearance in a shared lane is a fixed 3 feet to the side. [A01]
Why it matters: group space cushion; difficulty two; confusable sec06-F06 versus sec06-F14.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R03 | anchor: A01
Looking about one city block ahead is the scanning rule, and it is separate from the seconds-based count used for following distance. [A01]
Why it matters: group scanning; difficulty two; confusable sec06-F01 versus sec06-F06.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R04 | anchor: A01
A tailgater is handled by slowing gradually and adding space ahead of you, which lets you brake more gently when you must stop [A01] [A02].
Why it matters: group tailgaters; difficulty two; prereq sec06-F16.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R05 | anchor: A02
Your own blind spots are cleared with a shoulder check, while other drivers' blind spots are avoided by speeding up or dropping back. [A02]
Why it matters: group blind spots; difficulty two; confusable sec06-F23 versus sec06-F21.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-R06 | anchor: A02
The turn-signal distance is 100 feet, which the manual puts at about 4 seconds of driving. [A02]
Why it matters: group signaling; difficulty two; prereq sec06-F29.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-R07 | anchor: A02
For a turn just past an intersection you hold the signal until you are inside the intersection, the opposite of the usual rule to signal well ahead. [A02]
Why it matters: group signaling; difficulty three; confusable sec06-F30 versus sec06-F29.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-R08 | anchor: A02
Entering from a private drive means stopping and waiting for a clear gap, and another driver's blinking signal does not create that gap. [A02]
Why it matters: group entering traffic; difficulty two; confusable sec06-F24 versus sec06-F25.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-R09 | anchor: A03
Hand signals add one case the turn-signal list does not: signaling before you slow down or stop suddenly. [A03]
Why it matters: group signaling; difficulty two; prereq sec06-F36.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec06-R10 | anchor: A03
Normal passing is on the left; passing on the right needs both safety and a listed condition such as a driver ahead who is turning left. [A03]
Why it matters: group passing; difficulty three; confusable sec06-F37 versus sec06-F42.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec06-R11 | anchor: A03
The cue for returning to the right lane is seeing the whole front or both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. [A03]
Why it matters: group passing; difficulty two; prereq sec06-F39.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec06-R12 | anchor: A03
Being passed calls for moving right when it is safe and letting the other vehicle by; speeding up while being passed is never allowed. [A03]
Why it matters: group passing; difficulty one; prereq sec06-F41.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]
